# adrkit

> Decision memory for human- and agent-authored plans. adrkit turns architecture
> decision records into typed, machine-readable data that is enforceable in CI and
> legible to agents — without leaving git. Published as `@adrkit/core`,
> `@adrkit/cli`, `@adrkit/evaluator`, and `@adrkit/mcp` (v0.2.1 on npm), plus a
> GitHub Action at `mbeacom/adrkit/packages/ci@v0`.

Key facts an agent should know:

- A decision record is typed YAML frontmatter with a markdown body. The `affects`
  field declares what a decision governs (paths, packages, APIs, resources), which
  lets a tool answer "which decisions govern this pull request?".
- adrkit is deterministic and read-only where it matters: match resolution is a pure
  function, the MCP server makes no model or network calls, and nothing is approved
  automatically — it routes, and humans decide.
- The graveyard (`rejected` / `superseded` / `deprecated` decisions) is retrievable,
  so an agent can avoid re-proposing something already tried and turned down.

## Docs

- [Why adrkit](https://adrkit.dev/): the problem, the idea, and project status.
- [Quickstart](https://adrkit.dev/quickstart/): install `@adrkit/cli` and run `adr lint`, `new`, `explain`, `graph`, `migrate`.
- [Command reference](https://adrkit.dev/commands/): every command, option, and exit code.
- [Use in CI](https://adrkit.dev/ci/): the governing-decisions PR-comment Action and the ARB queue Action.
- [MCP setup](https://adrkit.dev/mcp/): the read-only `adrkit-mcp` server and its four tools.
- [JSON Schema](https://adrkit.dev/schema/): the canonical ADR schema, hosted at its `$id`.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/mbeacom/adrkit): the code, and the decision corpus that governs it.
- [README](https://github.com/mbeacom/adrkit/blob/main/README.md): the authoritative overview.
- [MCP server contract](https://github.com/mbeacom/adrkit/blob/main/packages/mcp/README.md): full tool contracts and limits.
